newsitem.title: UK: BOC launches synthetic liquefied air.
newsitem.headline: BOC launches synthetic liquefied air.

text.p: British industrial gases group BOC Plc said on Thursday it launched synthetic liquefied air commercially, the first company in the world to do so.
BOC told Reuters the breathable product could be used to create temporary cold storage spaces and to reduce temperatures rapidly, in warehouses and at rock concerts, for example.

The company said the gas, made by mixing liquid nitrogen and liquid oxygen, supported life, unlike the only existing alternative, liquid nitrogen. BOC said the product could result in sales of around 10 million stg a year in Britain. It is in talks with a number of potential users, including supermarkets. BOC said potential uses included cooling poultry-rearing houses in the summer and creating extreme air conditioning and test chambers for the aerospace industry.
The new gas will be made in a pilot plant in Oxfordshire, central England. A second British plant is scheduled to come on stream by the end of 1997.
